strengths: Identifies and addresses genuine gap in audio-text retrieval evaluation: standard benchmarks use caption-style queries misaligned with real-world search behavior
Thorough data leakage analysis revealing significant contamination (17.7% AudioCaps, 61.0% Clotho overlap with training data) and mitigation via leakage-free MECAT benchmark
Well-designed UIQ benchmark with linguistic motivation (five query types across three categories) validated by both human raters (9 annotators, 675 ratings, mean 4.15/5) and LLM evaluation
Novel hard negative discrimination metrics (HNSR, TFR, ∆-Rank) appropriately motivated and reveal limitations of standard retrieval metrics for exclusionary queries
Superior performance on uncontaminated T2A evaluation: OEA-Nemo3B 24.53% vs M2D-CLAP 23.55% R@5 on MECAT
Consistent empirical results across three backbone models (Nemotron-3B, Qwen-3B, Qwen-7B) from different organizations, demonstrating generality
Strong T2T retrieval performance: +22% relative improvement on MECAT (47.41% vs 38.74% R@5), demonstrating practical value for caption-indexed pipelines
Practical deployment considerations: reasonable online latency (2.3 ms/query) and parameter efficiency (0.29-0.36% of backbone trained via LoRA)
Reproducibility: detailed appendices with generation prompts, training specifications, and promised release of models, code, and benchmarks
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: OEA is straightforward application of LoRA to existing multimodal LLMs without methodological innovation; contribution primarily engineering-focused

UIQ benchmark carries significant synthetic bias: single LLM (GPT-5.1) for generation, controlled vocabulary constraints, only 13,053 queries, human validation on just 75 samples; paper acknowledges queries may underrepresent certain styles

Hard negative mining pipeline depends on MGA-CLAP and BGE embeddings for filtering, potentially biasing hard negatives toward examples confusable by these specific models; generalization to arbitrary negation patterns unclear
In-domain T2A performance degradation: M2D-CLAP 77.13% vs OEA 72.64% R@5 on AudioCaps; while data leakage explains discrepancy, it represents actual performance loss on established benchmarks
T2T and hard negatives are secondary contributions addressing narrow use cases rather than primary objective (T2A retrieval); over-presenting these as equivalent to main-task improvements
Missing ablations: no investigation of LoRA rank impact, projection head design, or component contributions; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
Substantial efficiency trade-offs: 15-25x increase in GPU memory (11.5-18.3 GB vs 0.6-0.7 GB); 5-7x slower offline audio encoding (163-667 ms vs 31-107 ms); limits edge deployment
Hard negative improvements claimed without explicit training, but hard negative queries ARE part of evaluation benchmark; generalization beyond current benchmark unclear
Limited scope: English-only evaluation; no cross-domain transfer experiments; no evaluation on other audio-text applications (music retrieval, captioning)
Incomplete specification of hard negative filtering thresholds and UIQ generation constraints (±2 word constraint lacks justification); some experimental choices not ablated

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifies legitimate gap between caption-style benchmarks and real-world search behavior (1.8 token average per Weck & Font 2024)
Rigorous data leakage analysis: Systematic documentation of 17.7% AudioCaps and 61.0% Clotho overlap with WavCaps, responsibly evaluates on contamination-free MECAT benchmark
Comprehensive UIQ benchmark: Five linguistically-motivated query types with both human validation (9 annotators, 675 ratings, mean 4.15/5.0) and LLM evaluation
Novel hard negative evaluation metrics: HNSR@k and TFR@k fill a gap that standard R@k metrics miss, addressing semantic discrimination ability
Thorough experimental design: Multiple datasets, three backbones from two organizations, detailed efficiency analysis, comprehensive appendices
Multiple backbone evaluation demonstrates generality: Consistent T2T improvements across Nemotron-3B, Qwen-3B, and Qwen-7B
weaknesses: Weak performance on primary task: M2D-CLAP achieves 77.13% R@5 vs OEA 72.64% on AudioCaps (-4.5%p); on uncontaminated MECAT only +0.98%p margin undermines core value proposition

Text-to-text results oversold: +22% T2T improvement is on secondary task (requires audio→text preprocessing) not aligned with primary audio-text retrieval goal; prominence in abstract misleads readers

Modest hard negative discrimination gains: HNSR@10 +4.3%p and TFR@10 +2.3%p absolute (34.7% relative masks small absolute improvement); mechanistic explanation about LLM negation patterns is speculative without empirical validation
Limited architectural novelty: Straightforward application of LoRA to existing multimodal LLMs; no principled justification for unified backbone superiority beyond vague 'LLM understanding' claims

UIQ benchmark limitations: Synthetic generation via GPT-5.1 with artificial ±2-word vocabulary constraints; only 75 samples for human validation; M2D-CLAP still achieves best average UIQ performance (47.76% vs 47.18%), suggesting UIQ doesn't measure coherent robustness dimension

Hard negative mining potential bias: Pairs created with MGA-CLAP and BGE embeddings then evaluated on OEA; both BGE and OEA are transformer-based, risking algorithmic bias; alternative mining pipelines not explored
Substantial efficiency penalty: OEA-Qwen7B 666.8 ms/clip audio encoding vs M2D-CLAP 58.1 ms (11× slower); 18.3 GB GPU memory vs ~0.7 GB (26× larger) limits practical deployment feasibility

Missing ablations and analysis: No ablation on LoRA configuration, projection head design, or linguistic analysis of negation handling despite being key claimed advantage; no significance testing or confidence intervals
Inconsistent model configurations: Different training recipes (with/without Clotho); variable gains across backbones suggest dataset-dependent tuning rather than architectural superiority
Data leakage context weakens in-domain claims: 61% Clotho overlap with training data means benchmark results are inflated; only MECAT is trustworthy where OEA's margins are thin

strengths: Identifies and rigorously quantifies significant data contamination in standard benchmarks (17.7% AudioCaps, 61% Clotho overlap with training data)—a critical finding that should influence future evaluation practices
Proposes comprehensive UIQ benchmark with linguistically motivated taxonomy and thorough validation (9 annotators, 675 ratings, comparison with real query distributions)
Introduces novel evaluation metrics (HNSR, TFR, ∆-Rank) that capture hard negative discrimination—an important dimension missing from standard retrieval metrics
Demonstrates generality across three multimodal LLM backbones from two organizations (NVIDIA, Alibaba)
Excellent experimental methodology with multiple datasets, detailed ablations, efficiency analysis, and reproducibility commitments (code, models, demo, benchmarks)
Well-presented paper with clear motivation, effective figures, and organized appendices
weaknesses: OEA does not improve text-to-audio retrieval performance on primary benchmarks (77.13% M2D-CLAP vs. 72.64% OEA on AudioCaps R@5)—undermining the core methodological contribution

UIQ benchmark relies entirely on synthetic query generation via GPT-5.1, introducing potential LLM phrasing bias; OEA's advantage on Imperative queries could reflect generation artifacts rather than genuine robustness; no real user query validation or search logs

Hard negative mining pipeline involves multiple filtering stages (MGA-CLAP embeddings → BGE embeddings → human verification of 'sampled pairs'); unclear if improvements reflect genuine discrimination or bias from mining procedure

T2T retrieval advantages (+22%) conflate improvements in text-to-text matching with audio-text robustness—two distinct tasks; doesn't directly address stated motivation of robustness in audio-text systems

Limited mechanistic understanding: hypothesized benefit from LLM negation exposure is not rigorously validated; no ablations on instruction-tuning or negation-specific pretraining to isolate causation
Narrow backbone dependency (requires multimodal LLMs with native audio—Nemotron-3B, Qwen2.5-Omni) severely limits extensibility compared to CLAP's flexible text encoder architecture
Significant efficiency trade-offs (11.5-18.3 GB peak GPU memory vs. ~0.6 GB for CLAP; 163-667 ms/clip audio encoding vs. 31-107 ms) with quantization mentioned but not demonstrated

Data contamination mitigation incomplete: MECAT uses auto-generated captions acknowledged as 'potentially noisier,' reducing confidence in absolute performance numbers and making generalization assessment difficult
Hard negative validation only on 'sampled pairs' with unclear sampling methodology; human inter-annotator agreement not reported; negative query ratings lowest (3.82/5.0) among UIQ types
Missing ablations: Why doesn't training OEA on UIQs improve further? Unclear which components (LoRA rank, projection dimension, training objectives) matter most

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing gap between caption-style benchmarks and real-world search behavior
Comprehensive UIQ taxonomy with five linguistically motivated query types across three categories
Novel hard negative discrimination metrics (HNSR, TFR) filling an evaluation gap
Thorough experimental rigor with multi-backbone evaluation, data leakage analysis, and extensive mechanism ablations supported by statistical testing (Wilcoxon p < 0.001)
Excellent reproducibility: code, checkpoints, benchmark datasets, and interactive demo released with detailed appendices
Important community contribution identifying data contamination (61% of Clotho, 17.7% of AudioCaps in training data)
Sound methodology with proper controls for ablations and convincing evidence that audio embeddings drive discrimination gains
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: OEA is primarily LoRA fine-tuning of existing multimodal LLMs without conceptual innovation
No clear SOTA on primary T2A task: underperforms M2D-CLAP on AudioCaps (72.64% vs 77.13% R@5, -4.49%p)
Critical UIQ validation gap: only 0.57% (75 of 13,053 queries) manually audited by humans; 99.43% of benchmark unvalidated, raising concerns about systematic generation errors
UIQ vocabulary grounding constraint (±2 words from originals) artificially limits query diversity to caption reformulations rather than exploring genuinely different search intents
Hard negative mining depends on single base model (MGA-CLAP) for acoustic candidates, potentially omitting confusion types outside its representational space
T2T dominance (+22% relative) requires caption pipeline, shifting problem from audio-text to text-text retrieval; practical importance not justified

strengths: Identifies genuine gap between benchmark queries and real-world search behavior, well-motivated by prior work
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with systematic data leakage analysis and thorough mechanism ablations revealing true sources of advantage
UIQ benchmark and hard negative mining pipeline represent valuable contributions for more robust evaluation
Honest reporting: ablations reveal that hard negative discrimination comes from audio embedding separability, not unique LLM negation understanding—strengthening credibility
Multiple backbone validation and extensive implementation details support reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: OEA is straightforward application of LoRA to existing multimodal LLMs; no architectural innovation beyond standard contrastive learning
Critical data leakage issue: 61% Clotho and 17.7% AudioCaps overlap with training data undermines main claims; on clean MECAT benchmark, OEA barely exceeds M2D-CLAP (24.53% vs. 23.55% R@5)

Circular hard negative evaluation: uses MGA-CLAP to mine pairs, then shows OEA outperforms M2D-CLAP on discrimination of those pairs; mechanism ablations reveal advantage is purely from audio embedding separability, not negation understanding

UIQ benchmark validation incomplete: only 75 of 13,053 queries (0.57%) human-validated; generated by single LLM with acknowledged potential bias; negative queries rate lowest (3.82/5); no comparison to real user query distributions

Weak on standard metrics: M2D-CLAP achieves best Avg UIQ (47.76% vs. OEA 47.18%—tied); T2A retrieval shows M2D-CLAP leads on AudioCaps (77.13% vs. 72.64%); OEA advantage restricted to imperative queries (instruction-following artifact) and hard negatives

Severe computational cost: OEA 11.5× slower than M2D-CLAP for audio encoding (666.8 vs. 58.1 ms/clip), 18.3GB peak GPU vs. 0.7GB, with only marginal gains on clean benchmarks—limited practical applicability
Concerning scaling behavior: retrieval performance saturates at 3B scale; 7B model shows marginal or negative gains, suggesting architectural issues and poor scaling

Mechanism ablation undermines core narrative: reveals 'order sensitivity is a general property of transformer text encoders'—OEA's edge is not unique LLM understanding but mechanical audio embedding separation

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Identifies genuine gap between caption-style benchmark queries and real-world search behavior with strong supporting evidence

Comprehensive benchmark contribution: UIQ dataset (13,053 queries) with linguistically-motivated taxonomy across three datasets; human validation (r=0.89) and LLM evaluation with documented inter-annotator agreement

Important methodological contributions: HNSR/TFR metrics address real limitation in standard R@k (measuring distractor suppression, not just retrieval); thorough hard negative mining pipeline combining acoustic and semantic filtering with human calibration

Rigorous experimental validation: Multiple strong baselines, proper controls (vanilla LALMs), extensive ablations (Appendix O) with particularly insightful cross-model controls; honest mechanism analysis showing OEA's advantage is audio-side embedding separation, not unique negation handling
Data integrity analysis: Thorough leakage detection (17.7% AudioCaps, 61% Clotho overlap) with MECAT as leakage-free alternative evaluation

Excellent reproducibility practices: Detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, promised code/checkpoint/benchmark release, extensive supplementary material with scaling behavior, efficiency benchmarks, and transparent limitation discussion
weaknesses: Limited model novelty and benchmark performance: Architecture is straightforward (unified LLM + LoRA + projection heads); critically, OEA underperforms M2D-CLAP on canonical AudioCaps T2A (72.64% vs 77.13% R@5); model advantages concentrate on T2T (requiring audio captioning) and niche hard negative discrimination rather than primary use case

UIQ benchmark validation scope: Only 75/13,053 queries (0.57%) receive human validation; single LLM generator (GPT-5.1) risks systematic biases; vocabulary grounding (±2 words) may constrain genuine variation assessment; no direct comparison against real Freesound queries (avg 1.8 tokens vs. UIQ 8-35 words)

Hard negative mining circularity: Stage 1 acoustic similarity retrieval depends on MGA-CLAP embeddings, creating dependency that may systematically miss confusion types outside MGA-CLAP's representational capacity; human calibration improves but doesn't fully resolve acknowledged limitation

Incomplete data leakage resolution: 61% Clotho overlap is substantial; MECAT uses auto-generated captions (noisier than human annotations); performance drops notably on leakage-free MECAT (e.g., 22.94% vs. 48.80% R@5), raising concerns about real-world generalization

Architectural constraints limit generalizability: Requires native-audio multimodal LLMs (hard constraint); only three backbones tested from two organizations; cannot extend to text-only LLMs without separate audio encoder; limits adoption and future extensibility

Unexpected scaling anomaly: 7B model inconsistently outperforms 3B variants (MECAT T2A R@1: 7.96% vs 7.74%), suggesting bottleneck is contrastive alignment quality, not model capacity; undermines argument that larger LLM backbone provides consistent benefits

Computational cost vs. practical applicability: Text latency 2.3-4.86 ms acceptable but audio encoding 163.8-666.8 ms substantially higher than CLAP (31.7-107.7 ms); deployment complexity with quantization; efficiency advantage over CLAP is limited
Query type realism concerns: Negative query format and keyphrase structure may not reflect actual user behavior; minimal evidence of alignment with real-world Freesound search patterns
